kill_fact: No kill fact found. I attacked the four load-bearing pillars of the bear/pass case against primary sources and each survived. COST-CURVE TRUTH: the company's own 2026-07-22 Q2 call states the operating cash cost per pound BEFORE by-product credits was $2.29 and the cost AFTER credits was $0.05, with a total by-product credit of $1,106 million or $2.24 per pound - the record's central claim that the near-zero headline cost is a by-product artifact, not a mining-cost improvement, is management's own arithmetic, not an inference. CYCLICAL-PEAK CHEAPNESS: the valuation guard is failing for the right reason. On live 2026-08-11 data SCCO trades at 16.39x TTM EV/EBITDA against Freeport at 11.62x and Teck at 7.45x, and the denominator is itself a peak - the Q2 LME copper average was $6.04/lb versus $4.32 a year earlier, silver $73.49/oz (+118%), molybdenum $29.44/lb (+43%), zinc $1.57/lb (+31%), while EVERY product fell in volume (copper -3.5%, moly -11%, silver -4%, zinc -14%) and total operating costs rose $202 million. A 41% revenue increase on four simultaneous multi-year-high prices and falling tons is a price event, and the record refuses to capitalise it. VOLUME: management confirmed on the call that 2026 is 917,000 tons and that 2027 copper will be 'more or less the same', so the third-consecutive-flat-to-down-year claim is verbatim guidance. BALANCE SHEET / FCF: the record's $1.2bn net debt is correct on the filed 30-June-2026 balance sheet ($7,994.4m long-term debt + $534.4m capitalised leases - $7,329.9m cash and short-term investments = $1,198.9m); FMP's own netDebt field of $2,863.8m simply omits the $1,664.9m of short-term investments. And the record's data correction is independently confirmed: the Q2-2026 capital-expenditure sign IS flipped in the source feed (capitalExpenditure +$441.9m, freeCashFlow $2,430.4m), which inflates the TTM figure to $5,965.1m; computed correctly, TTM operating cash flow $6,736.9m less capex $1,655.6m = $5.08bn, an $883.8m overstatement - the record caught this before I did. HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER search found none that breaks the case: no reserve downgrade, no equity issuance (the $1.25bn 10-year 5.35% June note covers most of Tia Maria's $1.8bn), no royalty or streaming structure, and the permit/licence issues that exist (illegal miners obstructing Los Chancas; the El Pilar water licence, now renewed) are already netted to zero in the record's own parts valuation.
corrections: Four corrections, none of which moves the fair-value level. (1) STALE SILVER - load-bearing to the timing argument, not to the valuation. The record asserts silver 'trades at $60.14 an ounce today', 18% below the $73.49 Q2 average that produced the credit. Silver closed at $60.245 on 2026-08-04 (the record's as-of date) but has rallied to $64.92 on 2026-08-11, so the gap is 11.7%, not 18%. The record's own sizing of the hit (~$270m annualised on 9% of sales at near-100% incremental margin) should read ~$175m. The direction of the argument survives; the magnitude is a third smaller than stated. (2) THE PRE-CREDIT UNIT COST HAS ALREADY INFLECTED DOWN. The record repeatedly frames pre-credit cash cost as 'rising 12% in five quarters, from $2.05 to $2.29'. True over five quarters, but the company said on 2026-07-22 that the $2.29 was '$0.02 lower than the value for the first quarter of this year' ($2.31), a 1% sequential DECLINE driven by lower production and administrative cost per pound and higher premiums. The base case's $2.35/lb and the adverse case's $2.40/lb therefore both sit above the latest actual print - the record has penalised itself by ~$0.06/lb, worth roughly +$1.8/share, which is why I am not moving the level. (3) THE CREDIT COMPRESSION IS NOT A FUTURE EVENT - IT ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE WITHOUT DAMAGE. The record's forcing function says the credit reversal first meets the numbers in the late-October Q3 report. In fact the by-product credit already fell 7% sequentially, from $1,189m ($2.41/lb) in Q1 2026 to $1,106m ($2.24/lb) in Q2, and EBITDA still set a record and the shares still made highs. The Q3 print is therefore a weaker forcing function than the record claims; a single quarter of credit compression has already been absorbed. (4) AN UNSOURCED DATE. The catalyst note and forcing function state Tia Maria 'commissioning tests targeted for May or June 2027 ... (second-quarter 2026 call)'. That detail does not appear in the 2026-07-22 transcript, which says only 'hopefully in the later part of 2027'; on that same call a Goldman Sachs analyst noted the disclosure had moved from 'third quarter of 2027' on the prior call to 'second half' in this release, and management answered 'for now, we don't expect a delay'. Attribute the May/June date to an earlier call or drop it - the softening from Q3-2027 to 2H-2027 is the better-supported point and cuts the record's way. Two footnotes: company-reported adjusted EBITDA was $2,856m at a 67% margin versus the record's computed $2,849m/66.4%; and the 0.012 stock dividend declared 2026-07-16 has a record date of 2026-08-11 (today), which has already restated the 52-week range in the data feed (high $221.67 -> $219.04, low $90.11 -> $89.04) - the record's levels, struck against a pre-adjustment $195.475, correspond to about $98.8/$154.1/$215.4 post-adjustment, a uniform 1.2% that leaves every ratio in the record intact.
